terms.grammar: imperative of nōlō with an infinitive
evidence: Quint. 6.3.59: nōlī, inquit, tamquam assem elephantō dēs
terms.comment: The everyday prohibition of prose, gentle in tone: “don’t be afraid”, “please don’t shout”.

terms.grammar: nē with the perfect subjunctive, second person
evidence: Publil. Sent. (prōsa) T 8: Turpia nē dīxerīs
Quint. 1.5.50: alterum negandī est alterum vetandī
terms.comment: Firmer: the prohibition of rules and advice. Quintilian counts nōn fēcerīs for nē fēcerīs a fault, “since one denies and the other forbids”.

terms.gloss: mind you don’t …, be careful not to …
terms.grammar: imperative of caveō with a bare subjunctive, or with nē
terms.register: with the bare subjunctive, vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs
terms.comment: A warning more than an order; see careful, don’t fall (cavē nē cadās).

terms.register: vōx cōmica et poētica: Plaut., Ter., Verg.; not in classical prose
evidence: Plaut. Mil. 1345: Nē timē, voluptās mea.

phrases.english: It is I; don’t be afraid.

phrases.latin: nōlī, inquit, tamquam assem elephantō dēs
phrases.english: “Don’t,” he said, “do it as if you were giving a penny to an elephant.”

phrases.latin: Turpia nē dīxerīs: paulātim enim pudor rērum per verba discutitur
phrases.english: Never say ugly things: little by little words knock the shame out of things.

phrases.latin: vīcīnīs bonus estō; familiam nē sīverīs peccāre
phrases.english: be good to your neighbours; don’t let your household do wrong

eris.html: The perfect subjunctive has a long ī (dīxerīs, sīverīs), the future perfect a short i: Bennett; Allen and Greenough §169.d.

sources: Lewis & Short: nolo · Lewis & Short: ne · Lewis & Short: caveo
